S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S056.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
S056.description: Excessive anxiety and worry (expectant apprehension) occurring persistently about a number of events or activities.

subtypes.Chronic Worry: Worry occurs more days than not for at least 6 months.
subtypes.Generalized Worry: Worry is not confined to specific topics but spreads to various domains like work, school, family, and finances.
subtypes.Catastrophizing: Jumping to conclusions that minor mistakes or events will lead to irreversible disasters.
subtypes.Intolerance of Uncertainty: Unable to tolerate future uncertainty, trapped in 'what if' questions.

S057.name: Uncontrollable_Worry
S057.description: The subjective experience of finding it difficult to stop or control the worry.

subtypes.Failure to Control: Unable to regulate worry despite efforts to stop or distract oneself.
subtypes.Intrusive Worry: Worries suddenly intrude into the mind and interfere with focus while doing other tasks.
subtypes.Chaining of Worry: One worry triggers another in a chain reaction, escalating to catastrophic thoughts.

S059.name: Concentration_Difficulty
S059.description: Difficulty concentrating or mind going blank.

subtypes.Interference by Worry: Unable to focus on the task at hand because worries keep surfacing.
subtypes.Inability to Sustain Attention: Attention is scattered due to anxiety, making it hard to focus on one thing for long.
subtypes.Mind Going Blank: Suddenly the mind goes empty or white, and no thoughts occur.

S061.name: Muscle_Tension
S061.description: A state where muscles are continuously tense, stiff, and accompanied by discomfort.

subtypes.Neck and Shoulder Tension: Muscles in the shoulders and back of the neck are knotted and stiff, causing pain or headaches.
subtypes.Jaw Tension: Clenching teeth or tension in the jaw causing jaw pain or headaches.
subtypes.Generalized Muscle Aches: Muscles all over the body, including back, arms, and legs, are stiff, painful, and easily fatigued.
subtypes.Chronic Stiffness: Muscles remain in a constant state of tension and do not relax.

symptom.disease_info: Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) is characterized by persistent, excessive worry about multiple domains of life that is difficult for the person to control and lasts for at least six months, often years. The anxiety is typically accompanied by physical and cognitive manifestations such as restlessness, fatigue, muscle tension, disturbed sleep, and difficulty concentrating, and it causes clinically significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning. The course is usually chronic and fluctuating, with exacerbations during periods of increased stress and partial remissions rather than discrete episodes. It is distinguished from other anxiety disorders by its broad, non–situation-specific focus of worry (rather than circumscribed fears or panic attacks) and from mood disorders by the prominence of anxiety and tension rather than sustained low mood as the primary feature.

patient.personality: He is a methodical, detail-focused production veteran with a competitive streak who channels his energy into precision work, art, woodworking, and structured hobbies like home brewing and mindfulness practice.
patient.stressor: Approximately a year and a few months ago, Kristian’s plant underwent a major restructuring with new automated lines, reduced staffing, and a shift in responsibilities that left him simultaneously training less-experienced coworkers and feeling implicitly responsible for keeping production targets on track. The new system came with frequent equipment glitches, pressure from management to minimize downtime, and a constant sense that any mistake could lead to safety incidents or job losses for his team, which tapped directly into his conscientiousness and long-standing tendency to mentally rehearse worst-case scenarios. Over time, this persistent performance pressure followed him home: he found it increasingly hard to enjoy his usual outlets like woodworking, basketball, and art outings because his mind kept looping back to possible production problems, potential layoffs, and whether he had overlooked something on his shift, which began to strain his patience with his family and reduce his engagement in activities that normally helped him decompress. He finally sought psychiatric care after realizing that his ability to focus on the line and during safety checks had noticeably declined, he was re-reading procedures without absorbing them, and both his supervisor and his spouse had commented that he seemed “constantly somewhere else” and more irritable, raising his own alarm that his mental state was now jeopardizing both work performance and home life.
patient.chief_complaint: “I can’t seem to focus at work anymore—my mind keeps drifting and going blank, and it’s been getting worse over the past year.”

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: Most nights I crawl into bed exhausted, but as soon as I turn out the light my brain starts replaying the whole shift and imagining equipment failures, and I just lie there for hours, waking up a couple times in a sweat thinking about alarms going off on the line, so I never feel rested even if I technically get enough hours in bed.

S056.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
S056.description: Excessive anxiety and worry (expectant apprehension) occurring persistently about a number of events or activities.
S056.manifestation: It feels like my mind is running multiple disaster drills all day—if a machine hiccups I start picturing the whole line shutting down, people getting hurt, us missing targets, me getting blamed and laid off, and then I jump to bills, the kids’ futures, even stupid things like whether the deck I built is going to collapse, and it just never lets up.

S057.name: Uncontrollable_Worry
S057.description: The subjective experience of finding it difficult to stop or control the worry.
S057.manifestation: Even when I tell myself, ‘Kristian, knock it off, you’ve checked everything,’ within a minute another ‘what if’ pops up—what if I missed a worn bearing, what if the trainee misunderstood my instructions—and it snowballs until I’m stuck in this loop I can’t switch off, not at work, not watching TV, not even when I’m trying to meditate.

S059.name: Concentration_Difficulty
S059.description: Difficulty concentrating or mind going blank.
S059.manifestation: Lately I’ll be in the middle of a safety checklist or reading a procedure I’ve known for years, and it’s like my brain just shorts out—my eyes are on the words but nothing sticks, or my mind suddenly goes completely blank for a few seconds, and I have to start over again and again because I can’t hold my focus with all the worrying running in the background.

S061.name: Muscle_Tension
S061.description: A state where muscles are continuously tense, stiff, and accompanied by discomfort.
S061.manifestation: By the end of most days my neck, shoulders, and jaw feel like I’ve been clenching through a ten‑hour bench press, and my wife keeps pointing out that I’m grinding my teeth or hunched up even when I’m just sitting at the kitchen table or working on a simple wood project in the garage.
